correctness.rationale: The graph is exactly F_2(KG(5,2)): unordered pairs of distinct Kneser vertices joined by one legal token move. It has 45 configurations, 15 degree-4 and 30 degree-6 vertices, hence 120 edges. Deleting the last Laplacian row/column gives a concrete 44-by-44 integral matrix. Independently constructed the graph, computed its exact determinant 49253533675382566432014336000, and independently reduced that entire matrix over each prime-power ring for p=2,3,5,7,19. Local valuations were p2: 0^28,1^8,2^4,5^4; p3: 0^39,1^1,2^4; p5: 0^41,1^3; p7: 0^38,1^6; p19: 0^39,1^5. These align into the claimed invariant factors, their product equals the determinant, and the supplied full characteristic-polynomial computation is supported by the exact verifier source. The Smith reductions are exhaustive finite exact matrix calculations, not extrapolations. A separate conceptual derivation of each p-primary summand is not claimed.

value.rationale: The two-token symmetric square of the Petersen graph is a canonical configuration graph with nontrivial irregularity; its sandpile group governs recurrent chip-firing classes. The exact noncyclic abelian group is a natural integral invariant not fixed by a Laplacian spectrum or spanning-tree number. A 44-dimensional fully reproducible integer Smith computation adds meaningful arithmetic information, although it proves no all-graph family theorem.

final_claim: The exact Smith invariant factors of the 44-by-44 reduced combinatorial Laplacian of the 45-vertex two-token Petersen graph are 1^28, 2^8, 4^2, 28, 1596, 38304, 191520^3, and the spanning-tree count is 49253533675382566432014336000; the stated 45-degree characteristic polynomial holds.
limitations: Single finite graph, not a family classification.
No claim of complete historical priority; unindexed tables possible.
